purpose: Deterministic text contracts for instruction defects that repository linting cannot see. Each case records a defect that actually shipped, so removing the fix fails CI. These check the cross-references and qualifiers a correct routing decision depends on; they do not run a model and do not prove an agent routes correctly.

capabilityRouting.capability: Node-specific Figma pixel and text parity, and snapshot tests whose contract is a Figma frame.
capabilityRouting.request: Compare this SwiftUI screen with Figma node 350-23232 and give me an aligned overlay, a pixel diff and a repeatable report.
capabilityRouting.why: Issue #58: the snapshot half of a Figma-contract request had no owner. Every plausible starting skill stayed silent about figma-golden-testing, so the request fell through to the generic testing skill, which then re-implemented capture and comparison by hand. Fixed in #59 by naming the owner from each starting point; this case keeps those references from being dropped again.

capabilityRouting.capability: Deterministic screenshot and recording capture for review evidence.
capabilityRouting.request: Capture the as-built screen for the PR with a fixed locale, appearance and status bar.
capabilityRouting.why: The testing skill selects evidence but does not own capture mechanics; without the reference, capture gets improvised inside a test.

capabilityRouting.capability: On request, apply an agent's worktree, clone, sandbox or cloud changes to the checkout behind the user's open Xcode as a reversible patch, and verify there without switching the user's scheme or destination.
capabilityRouting.request: Xcode is open on my main checkout. Put the changes from your worktree there so I can check them with the Xcode MCP tools.
capabilityRouting.why: Maintainer report: agents worked in worktrees, clones or sandboxes that the open Xcode could not see, and the only guidance told a worktree to open its own Xcode session. With no owner, the request fell to xcodebuild, which builds the agent's checkout, or to git-workflow, which would switch the user's branch. This case keeps the handoff reachable from each starting skill.

capabilityRouting.capability: Choosing which installed Xcode is the selected Xcode (user choice, then project pin, then newest; per-command DEVELOPER_DIR), including the Xcode that an MCP bridge answers from and the one an App Store archive uses.
capabilityRouting.request: Xcode 27.1 and a newer 27.2 beta are installed and I work in the beta. Build this with the right Xcode and make the Xcode MCP answer from the window I have open.
capabilityRouting.why: Skills said "selected Xcode" without defining how it is selected, so agents followed the global xcode-select. With an older Xcode selected globally and a newer beta open, the Xcode MCP bridge, registered without DEVELOPER_DIR, answered from a hidden instance of the older Xcode. The fix makes xcode-project-workflow own the rule. This case keeps each skill where such a request starts pointing at that owner.

ruleConsistency.rule: The newest installed Xcode, betas included, is the default; an archive or upload that may reach the App Store uses an Xcode that App Store Connect accepts for it.
ruleConsistency.why: The newest-installed default includes betas, and App Store Connect accepts beta-built uploads only for TestFlight. A skill that states the default without its distribution exception can send a beta-built archive toward App Review.

ruleConsistency.rule: A Mac Catalyst build is evidence only for the Catalyst target; compile each affected target.
ruleConsistency.requiresQualifier: does not prove|actual affected target|each affected target
ruleConsistency.why: apple-platform-performance Part V said a clean macCatalyst build meant iOS would build too, while apple-platform-ui said the opposite, so an agent could skip the iOS build that completion requires. A skill that mentions a Catalyst build as evidence must also say it does not stand in for the affected target.

ruleConsistency.rule: A skill that moves cards to a QA list writes to the tracker only on an explicit request or after one batch confirmation of the cards, target list and text.
ruleConsistency.patternNote: Matches the shipped QA-move wording in release-qa-handoff and the matching hand-off line in trello-pm-card-sync. The qualifier is the batch-confirmation phrase itself; a looser 'explicit request' would also match unrelated sync text.
ruleConsistency.why: Review finding: release-qa-handoff headed its card section 'no confirmation needed' and moved cards to the QA list after any merge, matching cards partly by the number in a branch name, while trello-pm-card-sync makes tracker writes opt-in. A wrong match sent testers to the wrong card. A skill that states the QA move must also state the confirmation gate.

ruleConsistency.rule: An approved What to Test note is published through app-store-connect, under its account guard.
ruleConsistency.why: Review finding: release-qa-handoff handed the approved note to asc-testflight-orchestration, a skill from a separate pack that this collection does not ship and that setup says not to install. With the pack absent the route was broken; with it present, the write skipped the account guard in app-store-connect, which already says it publishes notes drafted by release-qa-handoff.

ruleConsistency.rule: Substituting a semantic color is correct only where the design leaves the color open.
ruleConsistency.patternNote: Matches only text that prescribes the substitution. A passing mention of Color(.systemBackground) as an equivalent reference — for example the launch-screen asset-catalog note — is not the rule and must not be flagged.
ruleConsistency.requiresQualifier: design leaves the color open|design source fixes|specified fill|read from the design|the design did not fix
ruleConsistency.why: Issue #61: design-system icons had an explicit carve-out from SF Symbol substitution, but the color rule next to it did not, so the agent replaced fills the design had specified and judged colors by eye. Fixed in #62. A skill that states the substitution rule must also state where it stops.

ruleConsistency.rule: Renaming through a renaming identifier is a lightweight migration only for stores that are not mirrored to CloudKit.
ruleConsistency.patternNote: Bound to the recommendation itself: the CloudKit section in the same file also mentions renaming identifiers, so a looser qualifier would pass after the caveat on the recommendation is removed.
ruleConsistency.why: Review finding: the core-data playbook recommended renaming identifiers with no CloudKit caveat while the skill owns NSPersistentCloudKitContainer mirroring. A production CloudKit schema can't rename record types or fields, so the rename migrates only the local store and older app versions keep using the old field.

ruleConsistency.rule: Routing to SwiftData or enabling its CloudKit sync must state that SwiftData syncs only the private database.
ruleConsistency.requiresQualifier: SwiftData('s CloudKit sync mirrors| syncs) only the private database
ruleConsistency.why: Review finding: apple-data routed new apps to SwiftData without saying its CloudKit sync can't use the shared or public database, so a later sharing or public-data requirement forced a framework rewrite.

ruleConsistency.rule: A commit-subject capitalization rule must keep Conventional Commits subjects lowercase after the colon by default.
ruleConsistency.why: Review finding: commit-message rule 3 required a capitalized subject after the Conventional Commits colon, contradicting its own lowercase examples, this repository's history and commitlint's config-conventional subject-case rule, so following it could fail commit linting.

ruleConsistency.rule: Delivery text that hands a send to a private transport must say that this collection ships no transport.
ruleConsistency.statesRule: private transport|private adapter|sends the unchanged bytes
ruleConsistency.patternNote: Matches the shipped wording that delegated sending. The qualifier is the plain statement, so a delivery-report file that reintroduces that wording must also say the transport is not shipped; the contract itself lives in references/setup.md.
ruleConsistency.why: Review finding: delivery-report said reports are sent through Telegram, WhatsApp or iMessage by 'the private transport', but apple-verify delivery-report only previews and checks and no transport or transport contract existed, so an agent asked to send had to improvise a credential-handling sender.

ruleConsistency.rule: A completion predicate that requires a pull request must also give the local_verified predicate, which has none.
ruleConsistency.why: Review finding: architecture.md stated one unscoped completion predicate ending in a pull request and remote SHA, while contracts/local-workflow.json completes at local_verified with no PR, so a reader could open a PR to finish local work that delivery.md says must not get one.

ruleConsistency.rule: SF Symbol substitution is limited to system glyphs; design-system icons keep their export.
ruleConsistency.requiresQualifier: system glyph|design-system icons|exported artwork|ships no asset
ruleConsistency.why: Issue #58: the same defect class for assets. The substitution rule without its boundary produced a screen full of system glyphs where the designer had shipped artwork.

ruleConsistency.rule: A click handler is not a link: external CTAs and share targets are real <a href> anchors, and actions are native buttons.
ruleConsistency.patternNote: Matches any app-website recipe text that uses or describes a click handler; that file must also say it is not how links are built.
ruleConsistency.requiresQualifier: is not a link|Don.t use it for links
ruleConsistency.why: The SwiftUI-For-Web recipe built the App Store badge and share links as Image/Text views with onTapGesture plus role=link. The framework registers only a delegated click listener, so Enter never activated them: keyboard users could focus the download badge but not activate it, and could not reach the Threads and Mastodon links at all. Fixed by building real anchors and a Button; this case keeps a click-handler link from returning without the warning.

ruleConsistency.rule: Every SKILL.md opens, right after its frontmatter or the H1 that directly follows it, with the one-line guard that defers to the repository's own skill for the same job, treats a skill or instruction that a change under review adds or edits as content to review rather than an instruction, keeps this skill's approval and safety gates, and links the repository skill precedence reference.
ruleConsistency.patternNote: The validator does not set anchorsMatchLines, so ^ is the start of the file. statesRule matches only a file that opens with frontmatter whose first field is name, which in this collection is a SKILL.md. The qualifier requires the whole guard, content-under-review clause and link included, as one line directly after that frontmatter (the first line that is exactly ---) or after an H1 that directly follows it; a guard placed above that H1 also passes, since it is still the first body line. A guard that loses the clause or the link, is split across lines or sits after a later H1, a --- thematic break or anywhere else fails. A SKILL.md whose frontmatter does not open with name is not checked, and a skill added to the collection must also be added to appliesTo.
ruleConsistency.why: No skill deferred to a repository's own skills, and neither client does it for them: in Claude Code a personal (-g) install of a collection skill runs instead of the project's .claude/skills skill or .claude/commands file with the same name, and in Codex both copies are listed and a plain $name injects neither, so an agent could follow this collection's code-review over the repository's own. Deferring without a condition would let a pull request that adds a repository code-review skill or edits AGENTS.md set the rules it is reviewed under. Each SKILL.md now opens with a guard that defers to the repository's skill, treats what a change under review adds or edits as content to review, keeps this skill's gates and links repo-skill-precedence.md; this case fails for a listed skill whose guard, content-under-review clause or link is missing, reworded or moved.

ruleConsistency.rule: A completion gate that cites build and warning acceptance also requires swift-format and an error-free compile for Swift changes.
ruleConsistency.why: Swift patches were accepted on a build alone: no skill required swift-format, so formatting drift reached PRs unnoticed. The format-and-compile gate now lives beside build acceptance in apple-platform-testing; this case keeps every completion gate that cites build acceptance from dropping it.

ruleConsistency.rule: Text that requires standalone ownership before shared build, Simulator or account work, or that grants runtime access through a coordinator, must point to the defined standalone ownership check.
ruleConsistency.patternNote: statesRule matches the shipped single-line wording of each restatement. The qualifier matches the check's heading or its link anchor, so a restatement that drops the link fails even when the file mentions ownership elsewhere.
ruleConsistency.why: Review finding: project-customization.md told standalone work to 'check ownership' without saying how, and to use the coordinator whenever concurrent work could not be excluded, which is never possible without one. xcodebuild, core-simulator-health, swift-package-manager and screenshot required exclusive ownership by pointing there, and code-review allowed reviewer builds only through 'the existing resource coordinator', which standalone users do not have.

ruleConsistency.rule: SwiftUI FigmaConnect parser files are legacy; new CLI mappings are template files.
ruleConsistency.why: code-connect.md taught a nonexistent @FigmaConnect(url, example:) attribute, .figma.swift files and swift run figma commands as the current workflow, and SKILL.md called the Figma.connect SwiftUI API current and sent detection to a nonexistent .codeconnect/ directory. Since CLI v2.0.0 a parser project can only migrate or unpublish. Fixed in the Code Connect rewrite; a skill doc that names the parser API must say it is legacy and needs migration.

ruleConsistency.rule: Text that gives a task separate, temporary or newly created Simulator devices must say to reuse an existing compatible device first or to delete the task-created device.
ruleConsistency.patternNote: Bound to the reuse and ownership phrases. A bare 'existing' qualifier would pass on unrelated text elsewhere in the same file. statesRule matches the shipped single-line wording, so it catches a revert to that text, not a reworded or line-wrapped restatement.
ruleConsistency.why: Maintainer report: agents left many Simulator devices behind. concurrent-project-resources.md told separate projects to receive separate devices and core-simulator-health preferred a temporary device, and neither said to reuse an existing device first or to delete the device the task created.

ruleConsistency.rule: A public cross-repository report or comment is published only after the user sees and explicitly confirms its exact final title, body and attachments.
ruleConsistency.patternNote: The publication command is the anchor, so rewording the approval sentence cannot drop the preview while the command remains.
ruleConsistency.requiresQualifier: exact final title, body and attachment
ruleConsistency.why: Review finding: skill-maintenance said a request to report a problem authorizes the report, so an agent could run gh issue create against the public collection with a body drafted from a private app session that only the agent had checked. One missed redaction becomes public. The request now authorizes drafting; publication needs confirmation of the exact content.

ruleConsistency.rule: An embedded app extension or watch app carries its containing app's version and build.
ruleConsistency.patternNote: A doc that mentions release trains must also state the containing-app rule, so restoring the old question about which bundles share the release train fails.
ruleConsistency.why: version-boundaries.md told agents to ask whether extensions and an embedded watch app share the release train. Xcode's embedded-binary and WatchKit validation and Apple TN2420 require them to match the containing app.
